results.title: From everyday payments to stock trading: GCash shakes up local finance
results.description: For decades, the local stock market has been out of reach for the average Filipino as they rarely had the disposable capital that the wealthy have to open a traditional brokerage account, much less the financial literacy needed to navigate it. Little surprise, then, that it is essentially the private domain of family conglomerates, real estate empires, institutional funds, and high-net-worth individuals. GCash, the country’s leading digital wallet with more than 90 million registered users, is working to change that trajectory. Through its in-app brokerage feature, GStocks PH, GCash has evolved from a tool for everyday spending into a major force democratizing equity ownership—allowing users to trade Philippine stocks directly from their smartphones. Since its launch three years ago, GStocks PH has already onboarded 1.7 million users, representing around 53 percent of all online retail stock market accounts in the country today. With the upcoming record-breaking listing of GCash parent Globe Fintech Innovations Inc. (Mynt), the platform places a massive financial opportunity within reach of everyday Filipinos who once stood on the sidelines. Mynt is currently preparing for what is set to become the country’s largest initial public offering (IPO), aiming to raise up to ₱92.3 billion and surpass every previous listing record on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). The debut will bring one of the most successful homegrown fintech stories to the public board, following Mynt’s rise as the country’s first and only $5 billion unicorn. The company plans to offer up to 8.03 billion primary and secondary common shares at an indicative maximum price of ₱10 each. The base offer represents about 12 percent of the company, with the potential to rise to 13.8 percent through an overallotment option. PSE President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Ramon Monzon expects the upcoming debut of Mynt on Oct. 20 to drive strong market activity in an otherwise subdued year for the local bourse. “Considering that the IPO subscription will also be made available through GStocks in the GCash app, we expect to see a significant uptick in new retail investors,” said Monzon in a statement. By pairing a landmark public listing with an app already installed on tens of millions of phones, Mynt is creating a clear runway to cultivate an entirely new generation of Filipino investors through GStocks PH. Still, the debut arrives against a cautious economic backdrop, with the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) growing just 2.3 percent in the second quarter, which is a sharp drop from 5.4 percent in the same period last year. Headline inflation, meanwhile, is projected to average 6.1 percent for the year, well above the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) 2.0 to 4.0 percent target. Rising fuel prices, driven by renewed tensions in the Middle East, are also lifting domestic logistics costs and adding pressure on businesses and consumer's wallets. As a result, any decision to subscribe to the IPO will require standard fundamental analysis, particularly of how Mynt manages user retention, navigates heightened regulatory oversight, and defends its margins against competing digital banks and wallet providers. Yet for millions of everyday users nationwide, taking part in the listing means something more personal, as it gives them access to a stake in the primary financial engine that has turned the country’s digital financial inclusion aspirations into a genuine reality. This direct access to the local stock market is rewriting the broader narrative of the corporate landscape. What was once the private domain of the ultra-wealthy is slowly opening up to everyday Filipinos—right in the palm of their hands.

W.D. Gann Theory: Time Trading Strategy
results.description: W.D. Gann’s approach was built around one simple idea: price and time should be studied together. Instead of asking only “Where could price react?”, Gann also asked “When could that reaction become important?” 1. Price Level Start with a meaningful level: previous high or low, major support/resistance, or an important breakout area. A level by itself is not a trade, but it gives you a place to watch. 2. Time Window Gann focused heavily on market cycles and timing. In practical trading, this can mean watching whether price reaches an important level during a period where volatility or structure is already changing. The key idea is simple: Price Level + Time Window = Higher-Quality Area to Watch 3. Wait for the Reaction This is where many traders make the mistake. Gann theory should not mean predicting a reversal just because price and time line up. I still want confirmation: rejection candles, a structure break, momentum shift, or a clean reclaim of the level. A practical sequence is: Key Level → Time Window → Price Reaction → Confirmation → Trade How This Can Improve Trading The benefit is not “knowing the future.” It is becoming more selective. Instead of entering every support or resistance level, you wait for price, timing and confirmation to align. That can help reduce random trades, improve entry location and make invalidation clearer. 4. AURICVERSE Takeaway Gann Theory becomes useful when it helps you stop treating every level the same. ''Price tells you where. Time tells you when to pay attention. Confirmation tells you whether to trade.''

DC Kupwara reviews progress under HADP, JKCIP
results.description: Kupwara, Sep 18: Deputy Commissioner (DC) Kupwara, Shrikant Suse on Friday chaired a meeting to review functioning of Kisan Khidmat Ghars (KKGs) in the district and assess the progress achieved under Holistic Agriculture Development Programme (HADP) and Jammu and Kashmir Competitiveness Improvement Project (JKCIP). During the meeting, the Deputy Commissioner reviewed the operational status of KKG centres, with particular focus on their onboarding with Common Service Centres (CSCs), capacity building of Krishi Udyamis (KUs), delivery of services and revenue generation. A detailed assessment was also made of the district’s performance against the prescribed Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) under HADP and JKCIP. The review covered course completion by enrolled farmers, establishment of approved units, tracking of established units through the OTA application, utilisation of released funds, farmer and farm registration under KKG Level-2, completion of e-KYC under KKG Level-3, daily reporting by Krishi Udyamis, credit disbursement against sanctioned cases, sanctioning of credit applications, JKCIP coverage in selected blocks and approvals under the project. The Deputy Commissioner directed all concerned departments to adopt a coordinated and result-oriented approach to achieve the prescribed targets under each performance parameter. He instructed the officers to expedite farmer and farm registration, ensure the timely completion of e-KYC for all eligible beneficiaries, improve daily reporting compliance by Krishi Udyamis and strengthen credit linkages. The meeting also reviewed the implementation status of various interventions being undertaken under the two flagship programmes. Stressing the importance of convergence among the implementing departments, the Deputy Commissioner directed the officers to ensure the timely execution of approved interventions, undertake regular field-level monitoring and maximise outreach so that the intended benefits reach the farming community in a transparent and time-bound manner. The meeting was attended by the Chief Planning Officer, Lead District Manager, Chief Horticulture Officer, Chief Agriculture Officer, District Sheep Husbandry Officer, Assistant Director Fisheries and other concerned officers.

results.title: Sunita Ahuja hugs Kashmera Shah, Krushna Abhishek’s twin boys as they touch her feet out of respect
results.description: Mumbai, Sep 19 (IANS) Sunita Ahuja shared a heartwarming moment with her nephew Krushna Abhishek’s family as she arrived at his residence for Ganpati darshan on Friday. The visit saw Krushna’s twin sons, Rayaan and Krishaang, warmly welcoming their grandmother and touching her feet as a mark of respect for their elder. As soon as Sunita entered the house, the twins went up to her and sought her blessings by touching her feet. Sunita, in turn, showered affection on her grandchildren, making the festive gathering a special family moment. She later also greeted Kashmera and Krushna with the same love. For the occasion, Sunita looked elegant in a yellow printed saree with a red border, paired with traditional jewellery and flowers adorning her hair. Kashmera Shah opted for a blue embellished lehenga with a matching choli, while Krushna was dressed in a pearl white kurta. The family posed together amid the Ganpati celebrations at the residence. The family moment comes a few months after Sunita’s emotional reunion with Krushna and Kashmera on the reality show ‘Laughter Chefs Unlimited Entertainment’ Season 3. Sunita had made a surprise appearance on the show and met the couple’s twin sons for the first time after years of estrangement. Sunita had earlier spoken about the reunion, saying that she had decided to let go of the past and forgive Krushna and Kashmera. She described meeting her grandchildren as an especially emotional moment as the family rift had lasted for around 14 years. For the uninitiated, Sunita is Krushna Abhishek's Mami, the wife of his uncle and Bollywood superstar Govinda. –IANS rd/

results.title: Shipping 'must not become targets of geopolitical tensions': India
results.description: United Nations, Sep 19 (IANS) India, whose shipping and nationals have suffered collateral damage in the Strait of Hormuz conflict, has reiterated its call for respecting international law and said commercial maritime traffic "must not become targets of geopolitical tensions". "Navigational rights must not be subject to coercion, threats, unlawful restrictions or arbitrary interference", India's Permanent Representative P Harish told the Security Council on Thursday. "India is a major maritime nation, and we strongly support a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime domain", he said. Harish spoke at an informal Council meeting convened by Bahrain to discuss the maritime security environment under the Arria-Formula, named for Venezuelan diplomat Diego Arria, who initiated such gatherings while presiding over the body in 1992. India has also suffered economically from the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz, which disrupted the supply of oil and gas, as well as the steep rise in global petroleum prices. The disruption in the Gulf and West Asia "has implications across regions of the globe, particularly in terms of energy and food security", Harish said. He did not name the incidents or the parties involved in the attacks where India suffered collateral damage in the confrontation in the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and the US along with other Gulf Countries. India has protested to Iran and the US the killing of its sailors, and to Tehran also the attack on an Indian-registered ship. In April, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) gunboats fired warning shots at two Indian-flagged tankers. An Indian sailor was killed and another injured in Iranian attacks in July on two United Arab Emirates-registered ships. India protested both incidents with Iranian diplomats in New Delhi. In June, India called the charge d'affaires of the US embassy in New Delhi to protest the killing of three Indian sailors when the US attacked their Palau-registered ship. India, Harish said, has been contributing to maritime safety in the region's troubled waters by deploying its Navy. As of Monday, Indian security operations allowed more than 449 merchant ships carrying nearly 20.3 million tonnes of cargo or oil worth more than $8.4 billion to go through the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea, according to Harish. The disruptions in the Red Sea are by the Houthi militia, a Yemeni rebel group with Iranian affiliation. Indian Navy launched Operation Urja Suraksha in March with 11 ships in the Western Arabian Sea to protect maritime trade, he added. Several hundred Indian sailors are stranded on ships in the Strait of Hormuz because of the blockades by the two sides in the conflict. Speaking up for them, Harish said, "Seafarers must remain at the centre of our collective efforts. Their safety, timely evacuation, medical assistance, crew changes and repatriation require effective contingency planning and international cooperation." Harish drew attention to the new risks from developments in technology. New Delhi "recognises the growing importance of addressing emerging threats, including attacks involving unmanned systems, cyber risks and interference with navigation and communications", he said. "International cooperation, capacity-building and responsible use of technology will be critical in addressing these challenges", he added. --IANS al/rs

results.title: Jamaica undertakes external evaluation of public health preparedness
results.description: KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaica is undertaking a voluntary external evaluation of its public health preparedness and response capacities, under the International Health Regulations (2005) as the country continues efforts to strengthen national and regional health security. Chief Medical Officer (CMO), Dr Jacquiline Bisasor-McKenzie, said the International Health Regulations (2005) Verification and Evaluation Exercise (IHR-VEE) Mission provides an important opportunity for Jamaica to objectively assess its capacity to prevent, detect, assess, notify and respond to public health threats. She was speaking at the recent launch ceremony for the Mission, at The Jamaica Pegasus hotel in New Kingston. Bisasor-McKenzie said the exercise is particularly important, given Jamaica’s status as a small island developing state and a major regional and international travel hub. She noted that maintaining strong public health preparedness and response capacity is, therefore, not simply a requirement but a national imperative. “We view the VEE not as an examination that we must simply pass but as an opportunity to take an honest and objective look as to where we are, identify where we can do better, and strengthen the systems that protect the Jamaican population,” she said. The CMO welcomed constructive observations and recommendations from the evaluation team, noting that the identification of gaps should not be regarded as a failure. Instead, she said, it provides an opportunity to address weaknesses before they develop into vulnerabilities during a public health emergency. She also highlighted the importance of identifying good practices developed in Jamaica that could be shared with other countries as part of regional and global health-security efforts. Bisasor-McKenzie also underscored the importance of immunisation as a key component of public health protection. She described vaccines as among the most successful and cost-effective public health interventions, noting that they have saved millions of lives, prevented severe illness and disability, and helped to eliminate or control diseases that previously caused widespread suffering and death. She said Jamaica has a long-standing commitment to immunisation and disease prevention, with the National Expanded Programme on Immunisation playing a critical role in protecting generations of children and communities. The CMO emphasised that health workers are central to sustaining the programme, particularly because they are often among the most trusted sources of health information in communities. Their engagement, professionalism and ability to communicate effectively, she said, are critical to maintaining public confidence in immunisation. Bisasor-McKenzie acknowledged the contribution of the Ministry of Health and Wellness team, regional health authorities, public health professionals, laboratory personnel, immunisation teams and other partners to strengthening Jamaica’s health-security capacities. She also recognised the technical cooperation provided by international partners, particularly the World Health Organization and the Pan American Health Organization. She expressed the hope that the mission would facilitate productive discussions, frank exchanges and practical recommendations to strengthen Jamaica’s health security, protect its people and contribute to a healthier, safer and more resilient Caribbean. — JIS

results.title: ELPD to not release body-worn camera footage from August Harper's incident
results.description: The East Lansing Police Department (ELPD) will not be releasing body-worn camera footage taken during a use of force incident outside of Harper's Restaurant and Brewpub on Aug. 2, according to a City of East Lansing news release on Friday. While ELPD's Police Chief Jennifer Brown recognizes "the community's ongoing interest" in the case, ELPD has decided to not fulfill the public's requests for body-worn camera footage to prevent "jeopardizing the legal process." "ELPD will release the body-worn camera footage and any other relevant material when doing so does not undermine the ongoing legal process or an individual's rights," Brown said in Friday's statement. The use of force incident refers to ELPD's attempts to restrain Myana Collins, 20, during the early morning hours of Aug. 2. Collins was punched several times by a police officer while lying face down on the ground, handcuffed and restrained at the legs, as seen in a video circulated on social media. During the resulting investigation, one officer was placed on paid administrative leave, according to a news release on Aug. 3. As of Friday, the Ingham County Prosecutor's Office has finalized its review of the incident and has "declined to authorize felony charges." The case has been given back to the City of East Lansing's Attorney Office for "further review and possible charges."

results.title: Iran war's cost grows to $43.6 billion in new US military estimate
results.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. military's price tag for the Iran war has grown to $43.6 billion as of Sept. 3, according to a new estimate provided this week to lawmakers. The figure from U.S. Central Command, which oversees operations in the Middle East, offers the most up-to-date cost for the conflict since it was launched by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28. A Congressional Budget Office report released Tuesday said the war had cost $38 billion through Aug. 1 and will continue to rack up expenses of around $3 billion a month depending on the conflict's intensity. The new breakdown, seen by The Associated Press and reported earlier by Bloomberg and Punchbowl News, also showed the continued use of expensive munitions by American forces. Weapons costs jumped by more than $6 billion in just over a month, from $21.7 billion listed in the CBO report to $28.1 billion in U.S. Central Command's estimate. The financial cost is just one measure of the impact of the Iran war, which also is affecting oil prices and the stock market and has led to deaths and injuries of American troops. The political costs will be calculated in November's midterm congressional elections, with Republicans facing increasing headwinds from the war's unpopularity. The latest cost estimate has emerged as the Trump administration pushes for a historic $1.5 trillion military budget proposal. The White House also is asking Congress to approve a $95 billion package that would help fund the Iran war and other priorities. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called for the budget's passage during a speech Friday in Austin, Texas, at Saronic Technologies, which makes drones for the Navy. "We're asking for $1.5 trillion in the current budget to make generational investments to keep our country strong and sustain good, high-paying jobs for American manufacturers like Saronic," Hegseth said. "We will deliver on this generational investment. We will fund this department." Meanwhile, Democratic senators are demanding that Hegseth provide a full accounting of the costs of the Iran war. In a letter to the Pentagon chief, the lawmakers criticized the Defense Department for withholding basic budget information from Congress and the American public even as U.S. casualties and taxpayer costs increase. The U.S. military's one-page breakdown to Congress this week includes costs for operating warships, planes and bases as well as for equipment losses and medical support for troops. Casualties tallied by the Pentagon have included 18 dead and more than 830 wounded, according to the Defense Casualty Analysis System. The report does not include damage to U.S. bases in the Middle East, which the Islamic Republic has attacked with ballistic missiles and drones. A report from the Pentagon inspector general released Monday said Iranian strikes have damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures at U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan. In the new report to Congress, the figure for munitions was by far the largest, constituting well over half of all costs. The advanced weapons that have been in the most demand are defensive missile interceptors, such as those launched by the Army's Patriot and THAAD systems. The diminished stockpiles also have caused alarm in Europe, where U.S. and NATO officials have told the AP that there is a "beyond critical" shortage of missile interceptors. Saudi Arabia also is running low on interceptors and has turned to regional and Western allies for assistance as its standoff with Houthi rebels in Yemen drags on.
